author: Reedear
title: Nice game so far, but greed is coming
content:
It’s so funny, yet predictable, and like clockwork. They start off normal (the boosters cost just 900 coins yesterday) and, now, they’re 1500 coins today. The power of an update, lol. 
Watching the ads, you used to get just enough to cover a booster, so I’m guessing that’s why they had to up the price, or else you wouldn’t have to buy from their store too much. 
I see they haven’t changed that, yet, so I still respect that over the last game like this that I played (then deleted). I deleted that game because, like this one, it started out where you could watch ads and play without interruption for a bit, but then got to a point that you HAD to buy from their store to even play the game. I’m reasonable. I know games need to make money, I just hope I don’t end up having to delete this one, too. 
Can’t remember if it has ad free, but I think it did and I bought it, so no forced ads.
And after posting the update more, I’ve noticed I used to, maybe, have to buy a booster for one round. Now, they’ve made it to where I need to buy 2 boosters. Before the update, literally 2 days ago, I’d saved up 20k in coins from watching ads and playing the little thing they have every day, where I tend to win around 800 coins. Now that each boost costs 1500 coins and I keep having to buy them to play most rounds, I’m down to 11000. That quickly. Even watching ads and playing the little contest thing hasn’t been keeping up with how much I have to buy boosters now. Guess I’ll have to find a similar game that hasn’t fallen to greed yet.

Okay, I’m gone. The boosters went up in price (one is now 1900 coins) and, now, there’s a mode that puts blocks into play for you. It literally makes playing hard because you don’t even have a choice in how you play, by picking the block you want to play. I basically played this game until all my coins were gone, which didn’t take long because I had to buy so many boosters with my coins to actually play. And I played a lot. Got over level 450. Greed ALWAYS ruins these mobile games.

author: Caleb.2reall
title: Changed Beyond Completion
content:
⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐

Food Hunt is easily one of the most fun and addictive games I’ve played in a long time. I downloaded it expecting something simple to pass the time, but it ended up becoming one of those games I keep coming back to every single day. From the moment I started playing, I could tell that a lot of thought and effort went into making the experience enjoyable. The gameplay is easy to understand, but there’s enough depth and challenge to keep things interesting as you continue progressing. It’s one of those rare games that’s simple enough for anyone to pick up but still rewarding for players who want to improve and master it.

One of my favorite things about Food Hunt is how satisfying the progression feels. Every session feels like you’re working toward something, whether it’s unlocking new items, improving your skills, or simply trying to beat your previous score. The game constantly gives you reasons to keep playing without making it feel repetitive. Every match feels fresh, and I always find myself saying, “Just one more game,” only to realize I’ve been playing for another hour.

The visuals are fantastic as well. Everything is colorful, clean, and polished, and the food designs are surprisingly detailed and creative. The animations are smooth, the environments look great, and the overall presentation gives the game a lot of personality. It’s clear that the developers paid attention to the little details, and those details really make a difference. The sound effects and music also fit the game perfectly, creating a relaxing but exciting atmosphere that makes the gameplay even more enjoyable.

Another thing I appreciate is how well balanced everything feels. The game provides a fair challenge without becoming frustrating. As you improve, you genuinely feel yourself getting better instead of simply relying on luck. That’s something many mobile games struggle with, but Food Hunt does an excellent job of rewarding practice and smart decision-making.

The controls deserve a special mention because they’re incredibly responsive and intuitive. I never felt like I lost because of awkward controls or glitches. Everything feels smooth and reliable, which makes the overall experience much more enjoyable. Whether you’re playing for just a few minutes or settling in for a longer session, the controls make the game feel natural and comfortable.

I also love how accessible the game is. It’s easy to learn, but there’s always room to improve. That balance makes it appealing to both casual players and people who enjoy chasing high scores or perfect strategies. It’s the kind of game that you can recommend to almost anyone regardless of age or gaming experience.

Perhaps the biggest compliment I can give Food Hunt is that it respects your time. Every session feels worthwhile, and the game manages to stay entertaining without feeling like it’s forcing you into endless waiting or unnecessary interruptions. It simply focuses on being fun, and that’s exactly what it delivers.

The developers clearly care about making a quality game. Everything feels polished, thoughtfully designed, and well optimized. I’ve had a smooth experience throughout my time playing, and it’s refreshing to find a game that runs so well while still offering engaging gameplay.

Overall, Food Hunt exceeded every expectation I had. It’s fun, relaxing, rewarding, visually appealing, and incredibly addictive in the best possible way. It’s become one of my favorite games to play whenever I have a few free minutes, and I can easily see myself continuing to play for a long time. If you’re looking for a game that’s enjoyable, polished, and genuinely entertaining, I can’t recommend Food Hunt enough. It deserves every bit of this 5-star rating. Amazing job to everyone who worked on it—I can’t wait to see what updates and new content come in the future!
